segments.line: You have your phone, and your charger. Nothing else.
No signal. Not one bar. Your messages just spin, because there's nothing out there to connect to.
The first cellular phone network won't switch on until 1979. That's real.
GPS? The first satellite goes up in 1978. Your map shows a little blue dot, floating on a blank grey grid.
You try anyway. You climb to the top of the tallest building you can find, and hold the phone up to the sky. Nothing.
Just the wind, and a pigeon looking at you like you're crazy.
So the rules are simple. Everything that lives inside the phone still works.
Every photo, every song, every video you ever downloaded.
Everything that needs the internet is dead.
You open your photos. Your whole life is in there. Your friends. Your room.
Your dog, asleep on a couch that hasn't been built yet. You scroll for a long, long time.
And one more rule. The battery. One hundred percent. Every minute you use it, it drains. And in 1926,
charging it is not as easy as you think.
